arxiv-2107-02241.title: Revealing dynamics, communities and criticality from data
arxiv-2107-02241.creator: Deniz Eroglu 1,2,3, Matteo Tanzi 2,4, Sebastian van Strien 2, Tiago Pereira 1,2
arxiv-2107-02241.description: Abstract Complex systems such as ecological communities and neuron networks are essential parts of our everyday lives. These systems are composed of units which interact through intricate networks. The ability to predict sudden changes in the dynamics of these networks, known as critical transitions, from data is important to avert disastrous consequences of major disruptions.

arxiv-2108-04936.title: Using Information Theory to Measure Psychophysical Performance
arxiv-2108-04936.creator: James V Stone
arxiv-2108-04936.description: Abstract Abstract Most psychophysical experiments discard half the data collected. Specifically, experiments discard reaction time data, and use binary responses (e.g. yes/no) to measure performance. Here, Shannon’s information theory is used to define Shannon competence s^{\prime} , which depends on the mutual information between stimulus strength (e.g. luminance) and a combination of reaction times and binary responses.

arxiv-2203-09089.title: Birth and Death of One-dimensional Domains in Cylindrically Confined Liquid Crystals
arxiv-2203-09089.creator: Madina Almukambetova, Arman Javadi, Jonghee Eun, Juneil Jang, Cheol-Min Ghim, Joonwoo Jeong
arxiv-2203-09089.description: Abstract Nematic liquid crystal (LC) is a partially ordered matter that has been a popular model system for studying a variety of topological behaviors in condensed matter. In this work, utilizing a spontaneously twisting achiral LC, we introduce a one-dimensional (1D) model system to investigate how domains and topological defects arise and annihilate, reminiscing the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.

arxiv-2203-16629.title: A new parameterized monogamy relation between entanglement and equality
arxiv-2203-16629.creator: Zhi-Xiang Jin, Shao-Ming Fei, Xianqing Li-Jost, Cong-Feng Qiao
arxiv-2203-16629.description: Abstract We provide a generalized definition of the monogamy relation for entanglement measures. A monogamy equality rather than the usual inequality is presented based on the monogamy weight, from which we give monogamy relations satisfied by the α \alpha th ( α > 0 ) (\alpha>0) power of the entanglement measures.

arxiv-2208-12583.title: On the computation of the SVD of Fourier submatrices
arxiv-2208-12583.creator: Simon Dirckx, Daan Huybrechs, Robbe Ongenae
arxiv-2208-12583.description: Abstract Contiguous submatrices of the Fourier matrix are known to be ill-conditioned. In a recent paper in SIAM Review A. Barnett has provided new bounds on the rate of ill-conditioning of the discrete Fourier submatrices [ 1 ] . In this paper we focus on the corresponding singular value decomposition.

arxiv-2209-04642.title: LSDNet: Trainable Modification of LSD Algorithm for Real-Time Line Segment Detection
arxiv-2209-04642.creator: LEV TEPLYAKOV 1, LEONID ERLYGIN 1,2 , EVGENY SHVETS 1
arxiv-2209-04642.description: Abstract As of today, the best accuracy in line segment detection (LSD) is achieved by algorithms based on convolutional neural networks – CNNs. Unfortunately, these methods utilize deep, heavy networks and are slower than traditional model-based detectors. In this paper we build an accurate yet fast CNN-based detector, LSDNet, by incorporating a lightweight CNN into a classical LSD detector.

arxiv-2211-14297.title: Doubly robust nearest neighbors in factor models
arxiv-2211-14297.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . We introduce and analyze an improved variant of nearest neighbors (NN) for estimation with missing data in latent factor models. We consider a matrix completion problem with missing data, where the ( i , t ) (i,t) -th entry, when observed, is given by its mean f ⁡ ( u i , v t ) f(u_{i},v_{t}) plus mean-zero noise for an unknown function f f and latent factors u i u_{i} and v t v_{t} .

arxiv-2304-01582.title: Unitary Coined Discrete-Time Quantum Walks on Directed Multigraphs
arxiv-2304-01582.creator: Allan Wing-Bocanegra, Salvador E. Venegas-Andraca
arxiv-2304-01582.description: Abstract Unitary Coined Discrete-Time Quantum Walks (UC-DTQW) constitute a universal model of quantum computation, meaning that any computation done by a general purpose quantum computer can either be done using the UC-DTQW framework. In the last decade,s great progress has been done in this field by developing quantum walk-based algorithms that can outperform classical ones.

arxiv-2308-05249.title: A minimal model of fermion FIMP dark matter
arxiv-2308-05249.creator: Carlos E. Yaguna, Óscar Zapata
arxiv-2308-05249.description: Abstract We investigate a simple extension of the standard model (SM) in which the dark matter consists of a feebly interacting fermion (FIMP), charged under a new Z 4 Z_{4} symmetry, that is produced in the early Universe by the freeze-in mechanism.

arxiv-2407-20169.title: On separability in discrete geometry
arxiv-2407-20169.creator: Károly Bezdek and Zsolt Lángi
arxiv-2407-20169.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Károly Bezdek and Zsolt Lángi. A problem of Erdős ( [ 31 ] ) and a theorem of G. Fejes Tóth ( [ 27 ] ) initiated the study of non-separable arrangements of convex bodies and the investigation of totally separable packings of convex bodies with both topics analyzing the concept of separability from the point view of discrete geometry. This article surveys the progress made on these and some closely related problems and highlights the relevant questions that have been left open.

arxiv-2502-10522.title: GraphiT: Efficient Node Classification on Text-Attributed Graphs with Prompt Optimized LLMs
arxiv-2502-10522.creator: Shima Khoshraftar, Niaz Abedini and Amir Hajian
arxiv-2502-10522.description: Abstract . The application of large language models (LLMs) to graph data has attracted a lot of attention recently. LLMs allow us to use deep contextual embeddings from pretrained models in text-attributed graphs, where shallow embeddings are often used for the text attributes of nodes.

arxiv-2601-05731.title: A simpler and more efficient fixed point iterative scheme
arxiv-2601-05731.creator: Nida Izhar Mallick 1 , Izhar Uddin 2,∗
arxiv-2601-05731.description: Abstract 1,2 Department of Mathematics, Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi-110025, India. nidamallick2016@gmail.com, izharuddin1@jmi.ac.in. Abstract. Our work presents a new iterative scheme to approximate the fixed points of nonexpansive mapping. The proposed algorithm is constructed to enhance convergence efficiency while preserving theoretical robustness.

pmc-11460808.title: Effect of prophylactic corticosteroids on postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction
pmc-11460808.creator: Narinder P. Singh, Jeetinder K. Makkar, Bisman Jeet K. Khurana, Kunal Karamchandani, Mandeep Singh, Preet M. Singh
pmc-11460808.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). It is important to note that studies by Dieleman et al.,[3] Ottens et al.[4] and Sauër et al.[5] employed varying definitions and assessment periods for PNCD, leading to different outcomes. Specifically, Dieleman et al.[3] defined the occurrence of delirium as the use of neuroleptic drugs rather than the use of an assessment tool over 30 days, suggesting delirium might be under-recognised. Ottens et al.[4] determined cognitive outcomes by administering a battery of five neuropsychological tests at one month.

pmc-11489373.title: Unveiling the silent suffering: Examining the complexities of disclosure and concealment strategies in women living with obstetric fistula
pmc-11489373.creator: Sandra Freda Wood, Ebenezer Ato Kwamena Aidoo, Kweku Ewusie Orleans Lindsay, Jessica Afful Tuleassi, Frank Nukunu, Cindy Afoakwa-Acheampong
pmc-11489373.description: Obstetric Fistula (OF), one of the tragic birth injuries in developing countries, overwhelms women living with this condition with multifaceted effects. Although concealing has been justified in some studies, revealing is also encouraged. Such uncertainty leaves women in a loop of tension in managing the disclosure or non-disclosure of their diagnosis.

pmc-11519182.title: Ultra-processed food intake in toddlerhood and mid-childhood in the UK: cross sectional and longitudinal perspectives
pmc-11519182.creator: Rana E. Conway, Gabriella N. Heuchan, Lisa Heggie, Fernanda Rauber, Natalie Lowry, Hannah Hallen, Clare H. Llewellyn
pmc-11519182.description: Purpose(i) Characterize ultra-processed food (UPF) intakes in toddlerhood and mid-childhood, including identifying principal UPF sub-groups and associations with nutrient profile; (ii) explore stability and change in UPF intake between toddlerhood and mid-childhood.MethodsData were from children in the UK Gemini twin cohort at 21 months (n = 2,591) and 7 years (n = 592) of age.

pmc-12463114.title: Electrochemistry as a Tool for Redox‐Based Bio‐Information Processing
pmc-12463114.creator: Eunkyoung Kim, Chen‐yu Chen, Fauziah Rahma Zakaria, Dana Motabar, Mijeong Kang, Deanna L Kelly, Alessandra Napolitano, William E Bentley, Gregory F Payne
pmc-12463114.description: Redox, a native modality in biology involving the flow of electrons, energy, and information, is used for energy‐harvesting, biosynthesis, immune‐defense, and signaling. Because electrons (in contrast to protons) are not soluble in the medium, electron‐flow through the redox modality occurs through redox reactions that are sometimes organized into pathways and networks (e.g., redox interactomes).

pmc-12535271.title: Reliability of Ultrasound Features in Predicting Thyroid Malignancy
pmc-12535271.creator: Sushmitha D J, Rahul A V, Kiran Shankar
pmc-12535271.description: Introduction: Thyroid nodules have shown an increasing trend over the past years, with a recent surge. Ultrasound is the primary modality of investigation to detect malignancy in thyroid nodules, which is safe, cost-effective, and easily accessible, whereas fine needle aspiration biopsy is an invasive and costly test with risk factors.

pmc-12565461.title: Bordetella Pertussis in Children: A Retrospective Analysis of the Clinical Impact and the Role of Vaccination
pmc-12565461.creator: Elena-Roxana Matache (Vasilache), Gabriela Gurau, Valerian-Ionut Stoian, Andreea Eliza Zaharia, Manuela Ciocoiu, Nicoleta-Maricica Maftei, Paula Constantinide, Madalina Nicoleta Matei, Aurel Nechita, Dana Tutunaru, Pabulo Rampelotto
pmc-12565461.description: Pertussis, a highly contagious disease, contributes to a great number of hospitalizations among children, with an increased risk of morbidity and mortality. The aim of the study was to investigate the epidemiological and clinical features of B. pertussis infections among hospitalized children and to compare the clinical course according to vaccination status and the presence of co-infections.

pmc-13035871.title: An AI-powered research assistant in the lab: A practical guide for text analysis through iterative collaboration with LLMs
pmc-13035871.creator: Gino Carmona-Díaz, William Jiménez-Leal, María Alejandra Grisales, Chandra Sripada, Santiago Amaya, Michael Inzlicht, Juan Pablo Bermúdez
pmc-13035871.description: Analyzing texts such as open-ended responses, headlines, or social media posts is a time- and labor-intensive process highly susceptible to bias. However, large language models (LLMs) are promising tools for text analysis, using either a predefined (top-down) or a data-driven (bottom-up) taxonomy, without sacrificing quality.

pmc-13212913.title: A compatible gravity-driven organoid perfusion (GDOP) platform for drug screening with sensitivity and toxicity process evaluation
pmc-13212913.creator: Shun Wang, Xiaoliang Zhang, Houshi Ma, Linlin Lu, Huabin Jiang, Yuqiao Bai, Xiaoran Chang, Jinxian Wang, Tianhang Yang, Gangyin Luo
pmc-13212913.description: High-throughput experiments, unidirectional fluid replacement, real-time process monitoring, and simultaneous drug sensitivity and toxicity tests are hard to achieve on most existing tumor organoid chips. Here, we developed a gravity-driven organoid perfusion (GDOP) platform facilitating scalable throughput and supporting drug sensitivity and toxicity assessment on organoids.

pmc-13248002.title: Associations Between Patient Characteristics and Cartilage T1ρ Relaxation Times Vary Over Time Following Patellar Dislocation
pmc-13248002.creator: John J Elias, Lutul D Farrow, Richard Lartey, Ahmet Hakan Ok, Mei Li, Mingrui Yang, Carl S Winalski, Xiaojuan Li
pmc-13248002.description: The characteristics of patients that promote progressive cartilage degradation following patellar dislocations are not well understood. The study hypothesis is that associations relating cartilage degradation to low BMI, high activity and youth in the early months following patellar dislocation are not exhibited for contralateral knees or a longer time from injury.

pmc-13532767.title: Iatrogenic ureteral injury in colorectal surgery: a retrospective cohort analysis of risk factors and preventive strategies
pmc-13532767.creator: Giovanna Savoy PAZIN, Helena da Cunha Lopes de LIMA, Marcelo Lopes de LIMA, Wagner Eduardo MATHEUS, Claudio Saddy Rodrigues COY, Raquel Franco LEAL, Maria de Lourdes Setsuko AYRIZONO
pmc-13532767.description: Background: Iatrogenic ureteral injuries (IUI) are rare surgical complications in abdominopelvic surgeries, with an incidence varying between 0.15 and 1.0%. Aims: To evaluate the incidence of IUI in elective colorectal surgeries performed in a tertiary university hospital. Methods: This is a retrospective analysis of patients operated from 2004 to 2022, who presented IUI.

pmc-13710596.title: Factors associated with the nonperception of the need for care among parents of children who exhibit elevated scores on the strengths and difficulties questionnaire
pmc-13710596.creator: Stéphanie Bourion-Bédès, Aristide Boulch, Mario Speranza, Yvon Motreff, Bruno Falissard, Anne Pastorello, Alexandra Rouquette, The EpiCov study group
pmc-13710596.description: Too few children receive the mental health care that they need. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the non-perception of children’s mental health problem care needs among parents of children aged 3 to 17 years identified as having mental health difficulties (MHDs) and to explore the associated factors.

uslaw-usc-t40-s17307.title: 40 U.S.C. § 17307 — Purchase of insurance
uslaw-usc-t40-s17307.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t40-s17307.description: United States Code, Title 40 (Public Buildings, Property, And Works); Chapter 173 (Government Losses In Shipment). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. An executive department, independent establishment, agency, wholly owned Government corporation, officer, or employee may expend money, or incur an obligation, for insurance, or for the payment of premiums on insurance, against loss, destruction, or damage in the shipment of valuables only.
